aveline.name: Sister Aveline, the Chandler
lines_first: Another pilgrim? No — later than that. A Latecomer. The wax knows its own hours, and yours ran out elsewhere.

This is the Gray Cloister, keeper of the western vigil. I dip the candles that hold what's left of us. Six hundred a day, once. Now… you see the garth. Beautiful, isn't it. Try to remember it like this.

When you kneel at the lantern, child, the seeing ends and the surviving begins. What gutters will not rekindle while the Bellkeeper's grief drowns this quarter. Put him to rest — gently, if your blade knows how.
If you find candleglass in the dark, carry it to Osric — the Reliquary Smith, down among the bones below the basilica. He folds light into edges now. Me, I keep to wax and hours.
lines_repeat: Still walking, Latecomer? Good. Wax stands, wax serves.
The Bellkeeper was kind, before. He held the hours so the rest of us could let them go.

services.label: Buy the Tallow Heart — deepen the chrism flask — 300 orisons

sexton.name: Brother Ordo, the Sexton
lines_first: Mind the edge of the grave, Latecomer. I dug it true and I'll not have your boots spoiling the corners.
Six hundred brothers I put down, one at a time, while the choir sang the count. The singing was worse than the digging. The digging ends.
The Precentress? Past the screen, under the bell that never spoke. She won't stop for death. Death is an interruption, and she does not brook interruptions.
The west aisle came down in the ruin-hour. I can clear it — stone listens to me — but shovels eat, and mine eats orisons.
lines_repeat: Still above ground? Habit, or talent?
When it's your turn, I'll square your corners like the rest. No charge for craft.

services.label: Have him clear the west aisle — 180 orisons
services.done_line: There. The aisle runs clean in the dark now. Tell the rubble I said stay.

ferrier.name: Osric, the Reliquary Smith
lines_first: Mind the sparks, Latecomer. Bone burns quicker than you'd credit, and I keep my forge among six hundred brittle brothers.
Osric. I shod horses topside, before the guttering. Now I temper relics — the saints left good iron in their bones, and somebody ought to keep it sharp.
The Chandler sends her candleglass down the long stair and I fold it into edges. Wax remembers prayers; glass remembers LIGHT. A blade can carry both.
Work's honest down here. The dead don't haggle.
lines_repeat: Back again? Good. Idle iron rusts. Idle hands, worse.
Swing it till it sings wrong, then bring it home to me.

services.label: Temper the blade — 1 candleglass + 150 orisons
services.line_max: That edge holds all the light I can beat into it. The rest is your arm.
services.line_no_glass: No candleglass, no temper. The ruin grinds it out of broken windows — go shake some loose.
services.line_no_orisons: Prayers first, Latecomer. %d orisons, or the forge stays banked.
services.line_done: There. Hear it hum? That's the saints approving. Or the glass. Same thing, down here.

knight_morrow.name: Ser Adalric of the Morrow
lines_first: Well met, pilgrim! Ser Adalric — knight, votary, and incorrigible admirer of that view. Stand a moment. Look at her shine.
I came to keep a vigil of my own — a light that is MINE to tend. Grand ambition for a wandering knight, I grant. But reach for the light, friend, or the dark will reach for you first. Ha!
The kingdom turns on its memory like a coin — radiant, ruined, radiant again. Whichever face falls, hold to this: the Light was real. I have SEEN it. That makes us practically comrades.
If our roads cross again in some dim hour, call my name. Two lights burn back the dark better than one.
lines_repeat: Still walking! Splendid. The Light favors stubborn feet.
Magnificent, isn't she? I never tire of this terrace.

knight_crest.name: Ser Adalric, the Guttered
lines_first: …Oh. Another one still moving. Forgive me if I don't bow — the view is gone, and my reasons went with it.
I meant to keep a vigil of my own, you know. A light that was MINE. Look at it now. You cannot keep what was never yours to hold.
Go on — climb, fight, kneel at the little lanterns. It turns the world's coin over, nothing more. Heads, a memory. Tails… this.
The worst of it? I can almost recall how it felt, believing it mattered. Almost.
lines_repeat: Still here. Both of us. Imagine that.
If you find a light that stays lit — don't tell me. Kindness, of a sort.
